correctness.rationale: A connected 36-edge graph has a 23-dimensional cut space. Vertex switches act on all perfect matchings by a constant sign, giving 8192 unique representative signings. Direct exhaustive recursion proves 60 perfect matchings. The 8192-point integer transform and an independently structured signed DP agree on every multiplier, verifying the 9-level spectrum and full rank/nullity. A second exact Walsh transform of the zero-mask gives L1 mass 120192/8192=939/64 and 2412 supported cycle-space kernel entries. Translation averaging forces this projection norm to be minimal even for arbitrary real or complex projections. Direct pair counts yield precisely 128 zero two-edge characters and none at weight one.

value.rationale: The smallest cubic girth-seven cage is a canonical finite dimer ensemble, and its Fourier identifiability/optimal recovery problem is natural. The exact 9-level signed spectrum, 2112 vanishing gauge classes, first cancellation at 128 two-edge characters, and sharp endpoint projection norm 939/64 provide a complete recoverability and stability classification not implied by previously recorded unsigned matching and 2-factor invariants. This motivated finite exact invariant is worth knowing independently of an all-order generalization.
